A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SDR measurement and graded forced-choice study. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching Appendices A–F and the added Appendix G.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments with nine LLMs and 50 synthetic personas, plus original desirability-rating agreement and human-norm validation analyses in Appendices A–B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses and additionally reports corrected significance tests for the questionnaire contrasts.

M1.justification: The two-stage inventory optimization, 30 selected pairs, Likert and Thurstonian IRT models, SDR calculation, and recovery procedure are unchanged. Expanded explanations and model identifiers do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same IPIP Big Five inventory, synthetic-persona evaluation, and 100-adjective human-norm validation. Newly discussed deployment applications and narrative personas are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The Likert/GFC comparison, nine evaluated LLMs, and Speer et al. human reference remain unchanged. V2's explanation of persona targets as the central baseline describes the existing evaluation.

E3.justification: The 50-persona crossed instruction-by-format design, randomization, response scales, recovery metric, and IRT settings are retained. Provider-default decoding is newly disclosed, while the added significance tests do not change the evaluation design.

E4.justification: The agreement analysis in Appendix A and convergent-validity analysis in Appendix B are retained. No new ablation, robustness experiment, sensitivity analysis, or case study is reported.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 and Figure 3 add cell-wise paired t-tests with Bonferroni correction and significance markers. Existing confidence intervals, replication counts, and MCMC reporting remain unchanged; additional experimental runs are not reported.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports that all 45 Likert cells and 4/45 GFC cells are significant at the corrected 1% level. Existing heatmap effects, plotted SDR–recovery coordinates, and numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The scoring equations, SDR definition, optimization constraints, priors, and persona-generation mathematics are unchanged. The expanded explanation of ipsative scoring adds no new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same three contributions: IRT-based SDR quantification, a desirability-matched GFC inventory, and evidence of SDR attenuation with a recovery trade-off. Abstract and conclusion revisions preserve these claims.

C2.justification: V2 clarifies the normative interpretation of desirability ratings and the instructed-faking stress test. Sections 5.3 and 7 add guidance favoring Likert for honest persona recovery and GFC under evaluative pressure, explicitly scope applicability to persona steering, and discuss weaker signals from narrative personas.

D1.justification: New Appendix G and Table 4 disclose model identifiers, stage-specific query dates, and the absence of explicit decoding overrides. These supplement the existing prompts, optimization implementation, priors, and sampling details without establishing changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged apart from capitalization. Section 2 adds a limited conceptual refinement linking sycophancy to user-contingent desirability seeking and questionnaire SDR to broad social norms.

P1.justification: V2 consistently replaces trait-like terminology with response/profile language, expands selected explanations, and adds limitation subheadings, author emails, acknowledgments, and Appendix G. The main section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains significance markers and an expanded caption. Figure 4 replaces direct labels with shape, fill, and border encodings plus a model legend; Table 4 is added. Other displays receive limited sizing, labeling, and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through model and query metadata, supplements the existing effect sizes with corrected significance reporting, and gives clearer guidance on scope and response-format selection. The revised Figure 4 also makes model identities easier to distinguish. These provide useful, bounded improvements to reproducibility and interpretation while retaining the same core study.
